Implementation uses fetch with Accept: text/event-stream, reads response.body as a ReadableStream, parses SSE frames (`event:`, `data:`, blank-line delimited), pushes parsed events into the events array

Tests pass
userStories.notes:
Implemented. (1) `connectSse(baseURL, path = '/api/events')` opens a fetch with `Accept: text/event-stream`, drains response.body via getReader+TextDecoder in the background, and parses SSE frames split on `

` after `
` → `
` normalization. Field parsing follows the SSE spec (`event:`, `data:`, `id:`, comment lines starting with `:`, single leading space after the colon trimmed). Multiple `data:` lines join with `
`; missing `event:` defaults to 'message'. (2) `waitFor(predicate, timeoutMs = 5000)` polls events.find every 25ms and throws an error naming the last 3 `event:data` pairs on timeout. (3) `close()` aborts the fetch via AbortController. (4) Route is `/api/events?flowId=<id>` — flow MUST exist in the registry (returns 404 otherwise). userStories.title: REST integration tests — play, emit, SSE
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need integration tests for the runtime surfaces: triggering a node, emitting events, and streaming via SSE. These can only be validated across process boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend apps/studio/integration/rest.it.ts with a describe('runtime') block

POST /api/flows/:id/play/:nodeId — seed flow with a playNode whose playAction.scriptPath is a tiny tmp script that exits 0; assert response has runId and process actually ran (check exit via stub or via a later node:done event)
POST /api/emit — assert 200, idempotent
GET /api/events (SSE) — open via the sse-client helper, emit a node:status, assert it arrives in events array within 2s

External flow.json edit — write a modified flow.json directly to disk under the studio's workspace, assert SSE delivers a flow:reloaded (or equivalent — check watcher.ts for actual event name) within 1s
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) Watcher event name is `flow:reload` (NOT `flow:reloaded`/`reloaded`). Payload shape on success: `{ ts, valid: true, flow: <ResolvedFlow> }`; on failure: `{ ts, valid: false, error: <string> }`. (2) flow.json on disk uses the strict FlowSchema — `position` is split to style.json by splitFlow per NODE_STYLE_KEYS and MUST NOT be present at the node top-level when writing flow.json externally (every Flow*NodeDataSchema is `.strict()`). The external-edit test omits `position` so the watcher's reparse broadcasts `valid: true`. (3) For the play test: playNode requires `name`, `kind`, `stateSource`, and `playAction.scriptPath` must be relative under `<repoPath>/.seeflow/nodes/<nodeId>/`. addNodeImpl externalizes `detail` (creating the node dir as a side effect), then write the script under `<workspace>/<slug>/.seeflow/nodes/<nodeId>/scripts/play.ts` so resolveScript's realpath check passes. The script prints a single JSON line then `process.exit(0)`; runPlay parses stdout via JSON.parse, so the response body comes back as `{ hello: 'play' }`. (4) Open the SSE subscription BEFORE POSTing /play so the `node:running`+`node:done` broadcasts are queued; the SSE route writes a `hello` frame on subscribe — wait for it before triggering work to avoid a TOCTOU on broadcast registration. (5) /api/emit is stateless and idempotent — the broadcaster maps `status → 'node:running'|'node:done'|'node:error'` and forwards payload; calling three times in a row returns 200 each. (6) /api/emit requires the flowId to be in the registry (404 otherwise) so each test creates its own project first.

userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) Created apps/studio/integration/cli.it.ts covering every subcommand currently dispatched in cli.ts (24 unique commands + aliases): meta (--help/help/-h/--version/-v/version/unknown), projects+flows (projects:create, flows:list, flows:get, flows:delete, flows:layout, register, flows:register, flows:play), nodes (add/add-bulk/patch/move/reorder/delete), connectors (add/add-bulk/patch/delete), validate, e2e, lifecycle (start verified in --help, stop with per-test studio). (2) Shared studio per file (beforeAll/afterAll). (5) Output parsing: HTTP-passthrough subcommands print a single trailing `{"ok":true,...}` JSON line via printOk; `parseOkLine` picks the last non-empty line so human-readable headers (e.g. register's `Registered "name" → url/d/slug`) don't break the parse. userStories.title: Cross-boundary edge tests
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need explicit tests for failure modes that only manifest across process boundaries: SIGTERM cleanup, double-start guard, file watcher reload, parallel writes, stale PID recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Create apps/studio/integration/edges.it.ts (each test spawns its own studio — these manipulate process lifecycle so a shared harness would interfere)
Test: SIGTERM during in-flight nodes:add-bulk — fire request, immediately stop studio, assert process exits within 2s and flow.json is either complete or untouched (never partially written)
Test: double-start guard — spawn studio A on free port P, spawn `seeflow start --port P` again via runCli, assert exit code != 0 and stderr mentions the existing PID or port-in-use

Test: external file edit triggers SSE reload — connect SSE, writeFileSync a modified flow.json to disk under the workspace, assert the reload event arrives within 1s (event name and shape: read apps/studio/src/watcher.ts to confirm)

Test: parallel PATCH — fire 10 concurrent PATCH /nodes/:id on the same flow with different values, await all, assert final flow.json on disk equals exactly one of the input values (no torn write, no JSON parse error)
Test: stale PID recovery — spawn studio, SIGKILL it (no SIGTERM, no cleanup), then spawn a new studio, assert the second one starts successfully (stale PID file is cleared)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) `apps/studio/integration/edges.it.ts` — 5 tests, each spawns its own studio (no shared file-level harness because every scenario manipulates process lifecycle). (2) SIGTERM-mid-bulk: fires POST /nodes/bulk WITHOUT awaiting, then `process.kill(studio.pid, 'SIGTERM')` externally so the harness's `stop()` rmSync doesn't wipe the workspace before we can read flow.json. After waitForPidDead, re-read flow.json and assert `nodes.length` is either 0 or `bulkSize` (writeFileAtomic = write-temp + rename, never partial). (3) Double-start guard: foreground mode is what makes the second start actually try to bind the port — default daemon mode probes /health first and returns 0 with 'Studio already running', so PRD's 'exit code !=0' criterion only fits the foreground path. Bun.serve throws synchronously on EADDRINUSE; assertion: code!=0 AND stderr matches /EADDRINUSE|in use|already.*running|address.*in use/i. (4) External edit → SSE within 1s: same shape as US-007's external-edit test but with a tighter 1s timeout (watcher debounce is 100ms). Omit `position` on the on-disk node — strict FlowSchema rejects it (lives in style.json). (5) Parallel PATCH /position: fire 10 concurrent PATCHes with distinct {x,y}, assert all 200, then assert style.json's persisted position equals exactly one input verbatim (withFlowWriteLock serializes mutations; last-writer-wins). (6) Stale PID recovery: pass `home: mkdtempSync(...)` to both spawns so studio B sees A's pid file; SIGKILL A directly (NOT harness.stop, which would also rmSync the home); poll waitForPidDead; assert pid file content still equals A.pid (no cleanup happened); spawn B with same home; assert B.pid !== A.pid AND pid file content was overwritten with B.pid AND /healthz responds. Final teardown: `await studioA.stop().catch(() => undefined)` is safe even though home was already rm'd by B.stop (rmSync with `force:true` is a no-op on missing path). 5 tests / 37 expects / ~1.3s; full integration suite: 8 files / 77 tests / 481 expects / ~10.4s.

userStories.title: Add canvas data attributes for Playwright selectors
userStories.description: As a test author, I need stable DOM selectors on canvas elements. Adds three semantic attributes that benefit non-test consumers too (debugging, accessibility hooks).
acceptanceCriteria: In apps/web React components, add `data-node-type="<type>"` to every node component root for all six types: playNode, stateNode, shapeNode, imageNode, htmlNode, iconNode (grep apps/web/src for the existing node component files)

Add `data-canvas-ready="true"` to the React Flow root after initial layout completes (find the layout/ready signal in apps/web's canvas component — likely after first onInit or layout effect)
No production behavior changes; attributes are passive metadata
Typecheck passes

Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: run `bun run dev`, open the bundled example (e.g. examples/todo-demo-target or any flow with at least one node), open DevTools, confirm each rendered node has data-node-type, each edge has data-edge-kind, and the canvas root has data-canvas-ready after layout settles
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) Each node component already has a single outermost wrapper <div> — add `data-node-type="<type>"` next to the existing `data-testid` on each: play-node.tsx (playNode), state-node.tsx (stateNode), shape-node.tsx (shapeNode), image-node.tsx (imageNode), html-node.tsx (htmlNode), icon-node.tsx (iconNode). All six components live under packages/canvas/src/nodes/ — the apps/web canvas is a thin host that re-exports from @seeflow/canvas. (2) For edges, EditableEdge returns a fragment (BaseEdge + EdgeLabelRenderer portal + ViewportPortal); the React Flow wrapper `<g class="react-flow__edge">` is owned by xyflow's sibling render path. Solved imperatively in a useEffect that does `document.querySelector('.react-flow__edge[data-id=...]')` and `setAttribute('data-edge-kind', kind)` — mirrors the existing `data-handoff` pattern in the same file. `data.kind` is typed `unknown` (EditableEdgeData extends `Record<string, unknown>`), so narrowed via `typeof data?.kind === 'string'`. (3) For `data-canvas-ready="true"`, the canvas root is the outer `<div className="seeflow-canvas-root">` (packages/canvas/src/components/seeflow-canvas.tsx ~line 3942). Set imperatively via `wrapperRef.current?.setAttribute(...)` inside the existing `<ReactFlow onInit>` callback — avoids adding a new useState slot which would shift every hook-shim test's `useStateOverrides[N]` index per the CLAUDE.md note (12 documented slots). (4) Pure additive — no behavior change. Tests: full `bun test` passes (1580 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail), integration `bun run test:it:bun` passes (77 tests / 481 expects). Typecheck + lint + format all clean.

userStories.title: canvas.spec.ts — DOM + per-node screenshot baselines
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the canvas verification to assert every node type renders semantically AND visually, with baselines committed so regressions fail loudly.
acceptanceCriteria: Create apps/studio/e2e/canvas.spec.ts using the studio fixture from US-012

beforeEach: page.goto(`${studio.baseURL}/?flow=kitchen-sink`), wait for `[data-canvas-ready="true"]`, inject CSS to disable transitions/animations (`*,*::before,*::after { transition: none !important; animation: none !important }`)

Test 'every node type renders': expect .react-flow__node has count 6; expect .react-flow__edge has count 4; for each type in [playNode, stateNode, shapeNode, imageNode, htmlNode, iconNode]: expect locator(`[data-node-type="${type}"]`) toHaveCount 1, toBeVisible, not toHaveText('')
Test 'per-node visual baseline': for each type, await expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot(`${type}.png`, { maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02 })
Test 'connector kinds render distinctly': for each kind in [http, event, queue, default]: expect locator(`[data-edge-kind="${kind}"]`) toHaveCount 1

Generate baselines by running `bunx playwright test --config=apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts --update-snapshots` and committing the generated PNGs under apps/studio/e2e/canvas.spec.ts-snapshots/ (or wherever Playwright places them per config)
Re-running without --update-snapshots passes on a clean machine (verify locally)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: navigate to the kitchen-sink flow URL and visually confirm all 6 nodes and 4 edges render before relying on the spec
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) File extension is `canvas.e2e.ts` (NOT `canvas.spec.ts` as PRD wording suggested) — `bun test` default discovery picks up `*.spec.ts` everywhere, including under `e2e/`, and would try to run the Playwright spec via bun's test runner, which fails on missing globals. Playwright config sets `testMatch: '**/*.e2e.ts'` to scope its matcher to the new suffix. Snapshot dir is `canvas.e2e.ts-snapshots/` by Playwright's default convention. (2) URL is `${studio.baseURL}/d/` (NOT `/?flow=` as PRD suggested). The SPA's matchDemoSlug in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` matches `/d/` only. (3) Playwright must be invoked with `bunx --bun playwright test --config=apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts` — the `--bun` flag forces bun as the runtime so the harness's bun-only APIs (`Bun.spawn`, `import.meta.dir`) work. Default `bunx playwright` uses Node and fails on the first `Bun.spawn` call in studio-harness.ts. (4) Playwright fixture API requires the first argument to be a destructuring pattern (introspected to discover deps). Switched `async (_args, use) =>` to `async ({}, use) =>` with a `biome-ignore lint/correctness/noEmptyPattern` comment (Biome otherwise rejects the empty pattern). (5) `not.toHaveText('')` is skipped for `imageNode` — it renders only an `` element with no descendant text. The other five node types render their `name` (or html) as descendant text. (6) Web bundle (`apps/studio/dist/web/`) had to be rebuilt because the committed bundle predates US-011 and lacks the data-node-type/data-edge-kind/data-canvas-ready attributes the spec selects on. Committed the rebuilt assets so the spec is runnable from a fresh checkout. (7) Per-OS baselines: snapshots are named `-chromium-darwin.png` (macOS). CI runs on Linux and will need `-chromium-linux.png` — US-015/US-016 will deal with cross-OS baseline generation (Playwright Docker image or per-OS commit). The PRD's verify-locally criterion is satisfied. (8) `addStyleTag` injects the disable-transitions CSS after `[data-canvas-ready="true"]` attaches; combined with `waitForLoadState('networkidle')`, the canvas is stable before assertions run.

userStories.title: Orchestrator script + npm scripts + Makefile targets
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single command (`bun run test:it`) that builds the SPA, runs the bun-test integration tier, runs the Playwright tier, and exits non-zero on any failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Create apps/studio/scripts/test-integration.ts: (1) check apps/studio/dist/web/index.html exists and is newer than apps/web/src — if not, run `bun run --filter @seeflow/web build`; (2) generate runId = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g,'-') and export SEEFLOW_IT_ARTIFACT_DIR=apps/studio/integration/.artifacts/<runId>; (3) run `bun test apps/studio/integration/` capture exit code; (4) run `bunx playwright test --config=apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts` capture exit code; (5) write run.json summary to artifact dir; (6) exit with max(exitCodes)

Add root package.json scripts: 'test:it': 'bun apps/studio/scripts/test-integration.ts', 'test:it:bun': 'bun test apps/studio/integration/', 'test:it:e2e': 'bunx playwright test --config=apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts', 'test:it:update-snapshots': 'bunx playwright test --config=apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts --update-snapshots'
Add Makefile targets: test.it (calls bun run test:it), test.it.update-snapshots (calls bun run test:it:update-snapshots) — match existing Makefile style (## help comments, .PHONY entries)
Run `bun run test:it` from repo root succeeds end-to-end on a clean working tree
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) `apps/studio/scripts/test-integration.ts` — orchestrator that (a) freshness-checks apps/studio/dist/web/index.html against the newest mtime under apps/web/src (recursive readdir), rebuilds via `bun run --filter @seeflow/web build` if stale or missing; (b) generates `runId = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g,'-')`, creates `apps/studio/integration/.artifacts/<runId>/`, and exports `SEEFLOW_IT_ARTIFACT_DIR=<that path>` so any future harness consumer (and `run.json`) lands in the same dir; (c) runs `bun run test:it:bun` (the working glob, not `bun test <dir>`) via Bun.spawn with inherited stdio so test output streams live; (d) runs the Playwright tier; (e) writes `run.json` summary `{runId, startedAt, finishedAt, artifactDir, steps:[{name, code, durationMs}…], exitCode}`; (f) exits `Math.max(...stepCodes)` so either tier failing fails the orchestrator. (2) Playwright invocation: `bun apps/studio/node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config=apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts` — NOT `bunx --bun playwright`. The bunx path resolves against `~/.bun/install/cache/` and from REPO_ROOT picks up cached older versions (1.58.0 in this checkout) whose CLI surface differs (errors with `unknown command 'test'`). Even from `apps/studio/` cwd, the cached resolver was flaky. Using the explicit relative-to-STUDIO_DIR `node_modules/.bin/playwright` path + `bun` as the runner gives a deterministic invocation from any cwd and uses the package-local devDep (1.60.0). Both `test:it:e2e` and `test:it:update-snapshots` npm scripts use the same explicit binary path. (3) package.json scripts added: `test:it` (orchestrator), `test:it:e2e` (playwright only), `test:it:update-snapshots` (regenerate baselines). Existing `test:it:bun` kept unchanged. (4) Makefile targets added: `test.it` → `bun run test:it`, `test.it.update-snapshots` → `bun run test:it:update-snapshots`. Both have `## help comments` and are listed in `.PHONY`. Match the existing Makefile style. (5) Verified `bun run test:it` from REPO_ROOT: 80 integration tests / 490 expects / ~12s + 3 e2e tests / ~39s — orchestrator exits 0. run.json written to artifact dir as expected. (6) Full unit suite still passes: 1583 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail. Typecheck + lint + format all clean.

userStories.title: Land to main + tag + verify both deploy workflows pass
userStories.description: As the project owner, I need the entire integration suite landed on main and a release cut so both publish.yml and docker.yml actually run end-to-end against the new gating workflow. This proves the wiring works in production CI, not just locally.
acceptanceCriteria: All previous stories (US-001 through US-016) marked passes:true in prd.json before starting this story
Squash-merge or fast-forward the ralph branch into main (verify with `git log main --oneline -5` that all integration test commits are present)
Push main to origin: `git push origin main`
Bump apps/studio/package.json `version` field by one patch (current 0.1.41 → 0.1.42 unless higher already), commit as `chore(release): bump to v<new>`, push to main
Create and push an annotated tag matching the new version: `git tag -a v<new> -m 'Release v<new>'` then `git push origin v<new>`
Watch the resulting workflow runs via `gh run watch` (or poll `gh run list --workflow=publish.yml --limit 1` and `gh run list --workflow=docker.yml --limit 1` until both complete)
Both workflows must exit with `conclusion: success` — if either fails, fix forward (new commit on main, new patch tag) rather than skipping the gate

Verify image on Docker Hub: `docker manifest inspect tuongaz/seeflow:<new>` succeeds (or `gh run view <id> --log` shows the push step succeeded)
Append a release-verified note to ralph/progress.txt with the version, tag, and both workflow run URLs

userStories.notes: Requires gh CLI authenticated with permission to push to main and tags. Requires NPM_TOKEN and DOCKERHUB_USERNAME/DOCKERHUB_TOKEN secrets already configured in the repo (they are, per existing publish.yml and docker.yml).
